title: Customer Shell and Navigation Adoption
outcome: Existing NoorPath customer-facing routes use one canonical public, authenticated or transactional shell with consistent navigation, footer, breadcrumbs, support access and verified desktop/mobile reachability without changing domain behavior.
actor: Public visitors, authenticated NoorPath customers and booking owners using customer-facing journeys on desktop and mobile.
modules: Web owns shared public, authenticated and transactional customer shell composition.
Accounts continues to own authentication, session, return-to and customer authorization behavior.
Each existing domain module continues to own its page data, state and commands; the shell does not mutate domain persistence.
Design governance owns the approved Landing and Package visual authority, shared footer behavior, navigation terminology and responsive accessibility rules.
routes: Public visitor -> Landing or discovery -> canonical public header and full footer -> package and support destinations
Public visitor -> Package Details -> canonical public shell -> reservation entry and support
Authenticated customer -> customer shell -> Packages, My Journey, Help, Talk to Us and Profile
Booking owner -> My Journey -> journey detail -> documents, visa, cancellation and support
Customer -> OTP, reservation, payment or document upload -> transactional shell with compact legal/support footer
Protected customer deep link -> sign-in -> exact return destination when identity configuration is available
acceptance: Applicable live customer routes use exactly one approved shell variant: public, authenticated or transactional.
Public navigation exposes Packages, How It Works, Talk to Us and My Journey using valid destinations.
Authenticated customer navigation exposes Packages, My Journey, Help, Talk to Us and Profile without exposing staff routes.
OTP, reservation, payment and document-upload routes use a reduced-distraction transactional header and compact legal/support footer.
The approved full footer remains consistent across applicable public pages.
Breadcrumbs, back-navigation, active-page states and mobile navigation are consistent and keyboard accessible.
Every visible navigation control reaches its intended destination on desktop Chromium and mobile WebKit, or is recorded as BLOCKED_IDENTITY with an exact follow-up step.
The approved Landing and Package Details visual identity is preserved; this slice does not redesign page-specific content.
Customer, booking, traveller, payment, document, visa and cancellation domain behavior remains unchanged.
Foreign-account resources continue to return safe not-found behavior without resource-existence leakage.
Changed routes meet WCAG 2.2 AA expectations for keyboard, focus, target size, landmarks, text scaling, reflow and reduced motion.
No horizontal overflow, clipped navigation or inaccessible menu state occurs at supported mobile widths.
Rendered regression and navigation evidence belongs to the exact unchanged implementation SHA.
Product Owner approval is required before merge; production deployment remains separately approved.
policyDecisionsRequired: No new commercial, religious, financial or identity policy may be invented in this slice.
Existing approved pre-login and post-login navigation labels from improvement.md are authoritative.
Identity-dependent return-to tests remain BLOCKED_IDENTITY until Auth0 and real customer identities are configured.
exclusions: Staff portal shell adoption or operator sidebar redesign.
Customer OTP provider implementation or authentication-policy changes.
Booking-flow, occupancy, pricing, payment milestone or payment-provider changes.
Package builder, package publication or departure-management changes.
My Journey feature expansion, new downloads or new support-provider integrations.
API, database, migration, authorization-rule or domain-state changes unless a minimal presentation adapter is strictly required.
